verdicts.reason: A keeps the quote as the clear hero on one line, with the logo at top centre and the jar overlapping the warm circle on the right as in the original. Its flaws: a large empty gap between the quote mark and the quote, the attribution is very small, and the left circle floats empty. B inverts the hierarchy because the attribution is set much larger and bolder than the quote itself. B's logo wordmark also looks broken ('SOLST CE'), and the jar is pushed onto the grey circle on the left while the warm circle sits empty on the right.

A breaks the quote with an orphaned 'soon.' on its own line, and the oversized attribution outweighs the quote. A's logo is tiny and almost illegible. The jar sits awkwardly on the grey circle, leaving the warm circle on the right empty. B keeps the quote dominant on one line and keeps the logo readable and the jar with its circle. B's weak points are the dead gap under the quote mark and attribution text that is too small.

A has a readable quote as the hero, a centred logo and the jar kept as the key image on its warm circle. It still has a big empty gap below the quote mark and a tiny attribution. B shrinks the product jar and logo to near-invisible specks in the bottom-right, losing the key imagery and the brand mark. B's attribution also outweighs the quote, and most of the canvas is left as dead space.
